text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Dedicated pool eu-west-1 experiencing SLO degradation for model redwood-llama-70b. p99 streaming latency > 5s. Paging on-call.

sam.w: ack. jumping in. saw sharp spike starting ~08:12 UTC. p95 ~800ms, p99 ~5.2s on streaming. queue depth in dedicated-pool eu-west-1 = 347; hotshot queue ~78.

maya.p: console shows autoscaler requested extra slots but many warmups failed with handshake timeouts. host-level logs note NVLINK driver retries around the same timeframe.

kevin.t: region-only or global? any routing fallbacks triggered?

sam.w: region-specific to eu-west-1. routing policy attempted fallback to quantized-variant but fallback capacity was limited; many sessions were in-flight streaming which amplified tail stalls.

jenna: CS reporting multiple tickets. can we deprioritize non-critical tenants while we mitigate?

sam.w: applying deprioritize for freemium now.

ops-bot: command accepted: apply-routing-override --pool eu-west-1 --policy deprioritize:freemium --expires 30m

liam: autoscaler excerpt: 
```\n[autoscaler] 08:13:05 requested 6 slots\n[handshake] 08:13:22 slot 3 warmup failed: handshake timeout\n[kernel] 08:13:25 nvlink_err: retrying\n[autoscaler] 08:14:00 registered slots: 2/6\n```
looks like slow registration rather than outright provisioning failure.

maya.p: KV cache miss rate spiked during warmups too -> many cold KV paths at start caused extra token work and prolonged startup.

sam.w: immediate mitigations I'm executing now:
- enable emergency-burst (reserve capacity) for dedicated-eu-west-1
- manually spin up 3 hotshot nodes from spare eu-west-1b
- route streaming sessions older than 250ms to quantized variant (latency vs quality tradeoff)
- apply backpressure to batch pipelines

kevin.t: what's the emergency-burst command?

sam.w: ops-bot run emergency-burst --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --count 3 --force

ops-bot: emergency-burst accepted. provisioning 3 hotshot nodes. ETA ~120s.

jenna: CS: marking impacted customers as "latency degradation" on status page. preliminary count ~12 customers affected; 3 enterprise with SLAs.

maya.p: pushing partial reroute via edge to us-east fallback to avoid coldpool. cross-region adds ~40-80ms but avoids warmup delay.

sam.w: hotshot spin-up + handshake retries succeeded on 2 nodes after driver restart. after reroute + burst: queue depth -> 120, p99 down to ~1.1s at 08:18 UTC.

kevin.t: streaming stalls still visible?

sam.w: a few tail stalls remain. suspected causes: KV cache coldpath on newly joined nodes; handshake overhead for long-context streams.

liam: sample trace from a stalled session: 
```\nstreaming-handler: flush wait > 2000ms\nkv-cache: miss -> load shard 47 took 800ms\nruntime: token-gen blocked on kernel fallback\n```

jenna: need ETA for enterprise customers. propose message: "We are mitigating a latency incident in eu-west-1. Traffic is being rerouted and additional capacity added. Some users may see delays up to a few seconds." Agree?

sam.w: agree. posted status update. also added temporary cap on concurrent streams per session to 6.

ops-bot: safeguard applied: set-session-concurrency --max 6 --scope eu-west-1

maya.p: metrics after mitigations: p95 450ms, p99 950ms, streaming error rate dropped from 1.8% -> 0.2% over 4m.

sam.w: marking mitigated. keeping on-call window open 45m to monitor KV coldpath recovery. follow-ups:
- investigate autoscaler handshake timeouts + NVLINK driver flakiness on eu-west-1 hosts
- add KV pre-warm path for nodes joining pool
- improve routing fallback logic to avoid routing into warmup queues

kevin.t: I'll own autoscaler RCA. creating INF-6421 to gather handshake logs and host telemetry.

jenna: I'll lead customer RCA and coordinate CS comms.

liam: I'll prototype a short-term KV prefetch on node boot to speed coldpath where feasible.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: current responder sam.w will hand to maya.p at 09:00 UTC for follow-ups. Please acknowledge.

sam.w: confirm handoff to maya.p. logging timeline and commands executed in incident doc.

maya.p: ack. I'll run the follow-up checklist and coordinate infra for driver patching.

ops-bot: incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. p99 returned to <1s. Severity lowered to Sev2. Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-warmup-surge

jenna: tagging postmortem participants: sam.w, maya.p, kevin.t, liam, jenna. scheduling a postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

sam.w: note: longer streaming contexts exhibited worst tails. recommend tenant-level burst protections and earlier fallback to quantized variants in routing.

maya.p: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions appear. thanks team :thumbsup:
